subject: Manila microregion capacity: tiling design + deal-prioritization request
messages: From: Vanessa Ortiz To: Laura Bennett , Connor O'Brien , Marcus Lin , Karthik Iyer Cc: Date: 2026-08-30 09:12 PDT Subject: Manila microregion capacity: initial tiling ask Team — Quick context: Manila Labs (DL-2026-ML-0819) is ready to sign a 12-month Dedicated commitment contingent on a Manila microregion being available for low-latency inference for their core product (image+text multimodal routing). Their procurement lead wants a capacity design we can commit to in the SOW by next Tuesday. Immediate asks: - Laura / Marcus: can you propose a tiling layout (node counts + spare buffer) that meets 100ms 95p target for their typical 1.2k token, bursty routing workload? We should show sustainable and burst (2x) profiles. - Connor: what fallback lanes (EU/SG) and routing failover will you require? Include cold-start considerations and KV cache prewarm times. - Karthik: is Manila eligible for a soft-burst/tranche reserve or do we need a full dedicated tranche for their committed tier? I've attached a shallow traffic sample John shared (we have permission) and a skeleton SOW draft. I want a short deck by EOD Monday to share with John so procurement can start SOW review. Thanks — Vanessa Director, Strategic Accounts Redwood Inference Attachments: manila_node_tiling_v1.xlsx; SOW_ManilaLabs_draft_v2.pdf From: Laura Bennett To: Vanessa Ortiz , Connor O'Brien , Marcus Lin , Karthik Iyer Date: 2026-08-30 11:03 PDT Subject: Re: Manila microregion capacity: initial tiling ask Vanessa — See baseline tiling attached (manila_node_tiling_v1.xlsx). High level summary: - Sustainable profile: 8 tiles (each tile = 4xA10G-equivalent workers) sized for steady-state 95p < 110ms with prefix cache enabled. - Burst profile (2x): allocate a soft-burst reserve of 4 tiles (can be carved from regional burst pool in Singapore for the first 90 days while Manila racks are provisioned). - Spare buffer: 1 tile as a hot spare to absorb failover during upgrades. Risks/assumptions: - We need KV cache priming on dedicated node boot to avoid 500-700ms cold penalty for first requests. Plan ~8–12 min prewarm window per worker set. - If Manila racks are light on NVIDIA Ampere inventory, we will emulate equivalent performance with heterogenous SKU mapping — performance variability estimate included in sheet. Next steps: Connor to validate failover path latency numbers and confirm prewarm automation SLA. If all good, I will lock these counts into the SOW draft. Laura Principal Product Ops Attachment: manila_node_tiling_v1.xlsx From: John Reyes To: Vanessa Ortiz Cc: Manila Labs Procurement , CPO Date: 2026-08-31 00:47 +0800 Subject: Re: Manila microregion capacity: initial tiling ask Thanks Vanessa / Laura — Appreciate the quick turnaround. A couple of clarifications from our side before SOW: - Latency target: 95p ≤ 100ms for inference + routing (we can accept 120ms for short ramp periods). - Traffic shape: expected steady qps ~1800 (peak bursts to 4k qps for up to 10 minutes, 3–4x weekly). - Security: must support our KMS AES-256 key wrap; certification audit scheduled Oct. Any impacts on provisioning? We can sign a 12-month commitment if the SOW commits to the Manila microregion being the primary lane with SG/EU as failover and a 99.9% monthly uptime SLA for dedicated tiles. John Reyes Head of Infrastructure, Manila Labs -----Original Message----- From: Vanessa Ortiz Sent: Mon, Aug 30, 2026 at 9:12 AM PDT Subject: Manila microregion capacity: initial tiling ask > Team — > > Quick context: Manila Labs (DL-2026-ML-0819) is ready to sign ... From: Connor O'Brien To: Vanessa Ortiz , Laura Bennett , Marcus Lin Cc: Karthik Iyer Date: 2026-08-31 10:22 PDT Subject: Re: Manila microregion capacity: initial tiling ask John / team — Quick technical note on failover and warm caches: - Failover lanes: primary Manila -> secondary Singapore (same infra family) -> tertiary EU-West. Cold-routing to a different region will add ~60–120ms depending on KV cache state and model compilation warmup. - Prewarm plan: we can support automated KV priming via a light-weight traffic replay job that primes model weights and KV entries; estimate 10 min per worker slab. We need a pre-deploy hook in the SOW to run the job prior to go-live. - SLA and maintenance windows: we have an ops window policy (2 hrs/month) — we can carve an exception for Manila to keep monthly downtime < 5 minutes for planned upgrades during onboarding if procurement signs a priority dedicated tranche. (Will need legal signoff). I updated the latency_surface_diagram.png to show expected deltas; attaching. If procurement wants a hard 99.9% SLA with strict maintenance blackout, we should price an ops on-call premium (see pricing sheet line 7). Connor Senior Infrastructure Engineer Attachment: latency_surface_diagram.png From: Vanessa Ortiz To: John Reyes , procurement@manilalabs.ai Cc: Laura Bennett , Connor O'Brien , Marcus Lin , Karthik Iyer Date: 2026-09-01 08:05 PDT Subject: SOW draft and next steps (Manila Labs) John — Attaching SOW draft v2 (SOW_ManilaLabs_draft_v2.pdf). Highlights: - Committed capacity: 8 tiles (sustainable) + 4-tile soft-burst reserve for first 90 days. - Hot spare: 1 tile. - Prewarm automation: included as a delivery milestone prior to go-live. - KMS integration: we will support AES-256 key wrap; we will coordinate with your security team for audit evidence (SOC2 artifact pull). - SLA: we propose 99.85% monthly uptime in the SOW with a one-time ops premium option to reach 99.9% (pricing table attached). - Timeline: SOW sign -> 30 days for initial soft-burst enablement via SG pool -> 90 days for physical Manila racks (contingent on vendor capacity). Please review and call out any items that need to be explicit in the SOW (maintenance blackout, penalty clauses, data locality wording). Per John’s ask we will tighten the latency language to target 95p ≤ 100ms. If procurement confirms acceptance of the 30/90 ramp, I’ll generate the DocuSign and the PO path (we have the draft on the sign portal). Best — Vanessa Director, Strategic Accounts Attachment: SOW_ManilaLabs_draft_v2.pdf Related: https://app.sign.redwood.ai/doc/ML-SOW-2026 From: John Reyes To: Vanessa Ortiz , procurement@manilalabs.ai Cc: CPO Date: 2026-09-02 16:44 +0800 Subject: Re: SOW draft and next steps (Manila Labs) Vanessa / team — This looks good. Procurement is fine with the 30/90 ramp plan and the soft-burst approach for the initial period. We will sign the SOW pending the tightened latency commitment (95p ≤ 100ms) and the KMS audit coordination. Please send the DocuSign and PO instructions and procurement will return countersigned doc by Friday.
